subject.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns

question: Should OpenClaw make result-level yield a supported public Plugin SDK contract for plugin-owned external callback flows?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, additive, and well-proven, but it creates a permanent third-party API and sits beside existing approval and planned structured-question surfaces, so repository intent cannot be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Approve the narrow yield seam
options.body: Accept yieldToolResult as the generic handoff for plugin-owned external callbacks while leaving interaction state and UI with the plugin.

options.title: Route through interaction managers
options.body: Decline the result control and require plugin authors to use or extend approval or structured-question infrastructure.

options.title: Keep the seam internal first
options.body: Retain only the host-owned internal callback until another concrete external plugin validates the public helper contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow yield seam
recommendation.body: Accept yieldToolResult as the generic handoff for plugin-owned external callbacks while leaving interaction state and UI with the plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most strongly to both the extracted agent-core package and embedded runner architecture touched by the contract.
